headline: The chemistry Nobel goes to Kagan and Soai for mirror-image chemistry; Russia’s strike toll climbs to 20 and a ship sinks off Bulgaria; Berlin blocks Cosco’s Hamburg logistics deal.

stories.title: Chemistry Nobel goes to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for showing how chemistry can pick one mirror image
facts: Kagan (b. 1930, Université Paris-Sud, France) and Soai (b. 1950, Tokyo University of Science, Japan) share the prize “for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis”.
The puzzle: life is homochiral — proteins use only one of the two mirror-image forms of amino acids — yet ordinary reactions make both forms in equal amounts.
Kagan, 1986: a new way of steering reactions that produced a bigger excess of one mirror image than was thought possible (the “non-linear effect”).
Soai’s self-amplifying (autocatalytic) reaction, first described in 1995, made only one mirror image by 2003 — “other than life itself, no one had previously achieved this feat”.
The Academy calls the work decisive for designing reactions that make pharmaceuticals, where often only one mirror image has the wanted effect. Prize: SEK 12 million, shared equally.
stories.whyItMatters: A prize for a century-old origin-of-life question that also feeds straight into how single-mirror-image drugs are made today.

stories.title: Russia’s overnight strike toll climbs to 20 with a Pryluky apartment block hit; drones sink a cargo ship in Bulgaria’s Black Sea zone
facts: Material update to this morning’s card: Kyiv Post now counts 20 dead across Ukraine from the overnight and morning missile and drone assault.
In Pryluky (Chernihiv region, ~150 km east of Kyiv) a missile hit a five-storey apartment block; the regional governor put the toll there at 14, including four children, with 50 injured.

Zelensky: about 70 missiles plus drones, with energy infrastructure a key target; the air force says it downed 161 targets. Russia says it hit Fire Point sites that build Flamingo cruise missiles and drones.

Black Sea: drones hit two merchant ships ~80 miles off Bulgaria early Tuesday, the first attack on shipping in the NATO member’s economic zone. The Alfa Watan sank; all 18 crew of the burning Able were rescued.
Bulgaria has called off the Alfa Watan search with no survivors found and says the drones’ origin is under investigation; Zelensky blames Russia. Bulgaria’s Security Council meets this afternoon.
stories.whyItMatters: A sunk ship in a NATO member’s waters takes the war at sea closer to the alliance, on the same day as one of the deadliest strikes on Ukrainian cities this autumn.

stories.title: Berlin blocks China’s Cosco from buying 80% of Hamburg logistics firm Zippel
facts: Cabinet decision on Wednesday; the Economy Ministry will now issue the ban under the Foreign Trade and Payments Act.
Ministry spokesman: the purchase “would have deepened dependencies and endangered the resilience of Germany’s and the EU’s supply chains”.
The Bundeskartellamt had cleared the deal on competition grounds in February; in late April it emerged that the domestic intelligence agency (BfV) had concerns.
Zippel moves goods arriving at the Hamburg and Bremerhaven seaports by rail, ship and truck and has about 350 staff.
Cosco already holds 24.99% of Hamburg’s Tollerort container terminal — the stake was capped below 25% after a bitter coalition fight in 2022.
stories.whyItMatters: After the 2022 Tollerort compromise, Berlin now says no outright to Chinese control of port logistics, in line with its tougher line on China.

stories.title: Hanning fallout: MI6, GCHQ and US agencies review everything they shared with the BND
facts: New since yesterday’s arrest: per the Telegraph, MI6, GCHQ and several US services are reviewing all sensitive intel shared with European allies in the period, to protect agents and informants.

The accusation: after leaving office, the 80-year-old allegedly got ~2,000 secret documents via his former office head and wrote an analysis for a foreign intelligence apparatus; some came from partner services.

Federal prosecutors allege intelligence-agent activity, treasonous espionage and attempted treason; Hanning is due before an investigating judge today. His ex-office head was also arrested as an alleged accomplice.
BND president Martin Jäger: “no compromises” on internal security. The chair of the Bundestag oversight panel, Marc Henrichmann (CDU), says Germany now has to send clear signals to partner services.
stories.whyItMatters: The damage could reach beyond Germany: if allied sources were exposed, intelligence sharing with Berlin may cool for a while.

stories.title: Finland orders Google to stop work at two data-centre sites after 300+ hectares of forest were cleared
facts: The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) says work at one site went ahead without a mandatory environmental impact assessment; anything that would “significantly alter the environment” must stop by 23 October.
The order covers preparatory work at Muhos and Kajaani: removing trees and topsoil, building site roads and storage areas, and changing ditches.
Tuike Finland, the company behind the projects, must explain itself and set out next steps by 14 October or face enforcement proceedings.
Google: “We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance”; it promises tree planting across 130 ha at Muhos.
The sites are part of Google’s record €13bn Finland plan for 2027–28 (Kajaani, Muhos, Vaala plus Hamina) — its largest single investment in Europe.
stories.whyItMatters: The AI data-centre boom is running into Europe’s environmental rules on the ground — here less than a month after the investment was announced.

image.alt: An aerial view shows the site where Google's data centre is set to be built in Muhos, Finland.

stories.title: Japan raids Asahi, Kirin, Sapporo and Suntory over a suspected beer price cartel
facts: The Japan Fair Trade Commission opened compulsory, warrant-backed investigations on Wednesday on suspicion of violating the Antimonopoly Act.

The four control more than 90% of a beer market worth over ¥1tn a year and are suspected of coordinating the timing and size of price rises for beer, low-malt beer and beer-like drinks over several years.
According to reports, sales executives met after the monthly Brewers Association of Japan meetings to set wholesale price increases per litre and by container type.
The JFTC is considering a criminal complaint; all four companies confirmed the probe and said they would cooperate.

image.alt: Asahi Super Dry beers are seen on display at a supermarket in Tokyo on October 3, 2025.

facts.text: Thuringia’s premier Mario Voigt (CDU) withdrew his lawsuit against TU Chemnitz revoking his doctorate over plagiarism; he says the fight costs time he owes the state.

Cabinet passed Hubig’s digital-violence bill: up to two years for sexualised deepfakes (even for own use or labelled as AI) and harmful impersonation, up to three for sharing rape videos. Bundestag next.
France suspends stun grenades at school protests after a 15-year-old in Lens lost a hand; police inspectors are probing 18 cases, and 6,500+ people, mostly minors, have been detained.
Irkutsk lab death: Trump says he’ll talk to Putin “very soon” and report “probably” Thursday; Russia says everyone in contact with the 28-year-old tested negative and plague is unconfirmed.
Musk says Grok Bot will now use “the best back end model for any given task”, naming Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney and Suno — no terms or timeline given.
Sport Bild: BVB is leaning towards not renewing the Rheinmetall sponsorship (up to €10m a year) when it ends in summer 2027; Rheinmetall says it is happy and will decide jointly with the club.

facts.text: Next Bun ships `bun check`, a built-in TypeScript type checker written in Rust; a merged PR aligns it with `tsc --noEmit`. Jarred Sumner’s goal: ahead-of-time compiled JS/TS that rivals Go.
Atlassian CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS 9.3): unauthenticated reads of known files across eight self-hosted products incl. Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket and Crowd. Not exploited yet — patch now.
Outlook on the web and new Outlook will block .msix and .msixbundle attachments by default from early November (done by mid-November); admins can allow them per mailbox policy.

Svelte 5.57.2: patch release fixing event handlers assigned after a top-level `await` in production, async deriveds on components destroyed mid-await, and a missing error for doubled `{:else}` blocks.
